newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended up on Friday compared to New York's previous close as local punters covered short positions before the over-the-counter options expiry on Monday and holiday in Tokyo on Tuesday, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$340.90/341.40 an ounce against New York's US$340.50/341.00 close on Thursday.
"There was shortcovering in the Hong Kong market ahead of next week," said one bullion dealer.
Sources said players were keen to close positions before the OTC options expiry and the Japan markets holiday.
Hong Kong also saw some gold buying from Japan on currency movements towards the end of Tokyo trading.
The markets were relatively quiet as Sydney was closed, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$7 higher at HK$3,157 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -2.00 from its previous fix at -5.00
